title: engine: pin env (PYTHONPATH sitecustomize + DELEGATE_WORKFLOW_PIN) poisons python subprocesses of workflow children
description: Same family as the DELEGATE_WORKFLOW_LOCK_FD leak. PinRuntime.environment exports PYTHONPATH=<pin src> and DELEGATE_WORKFLOW_PIN to make nested delegate invocations stay pinned, and the supervisor passes both to every child agent. The pin src ships sitecustomize.py, so ANY plain python3 a child spawns auto-imports it at interpreter startup; seeing DELEGATE_WORKFLOW_PIN it imports delegate_agent from the pin store into sys.modules before test bootstrap code can prepend the checkout src. Observed 2026-08-31 wf_6a7ad997c63a: the wave-1 close agent's verify rows tested the pre-plan pinned runtime against post-plan tests — 11 false failures, close refused, run gated. Also: environment() PREPENDS to existing PYTHONPATH, so a resumed supervisor doubles the entry. Mitigated at the test layer (tests/__init__ evicts foreign delegate_agent modules and scrubs pin env, spine commit ba17857), but the engine fix is to scrub pin env plus DELEGATE_WORKFLOW_LOCK_FD from agent-child env: children get the pinned runtime via cli_argv, not env, and only nested delegate launches need the pin env — which the supervisor can re-apply at its own spawn sites. Related close-agent defect: a resumed close thread re-greps its previous attempt's /tmp logs instead of re-running rows, so a stale refusal replays; forcing re-run required moving /tmp/delegate-close-wave1-* aside.

title: workflow watchdog false fires: strict reader loses TOCTOU race against atomic heartbeat writes
description: ROOT CAUSE, verified live 2026-08-31. read_private_text_bounded refuses any file whose fstat shows st_nlink != 1. write_json_atomic replaces heartbeat.json/status.json via os.replace, so a reader that opens the OLD inode just before the replace fstats st_nlink == 0 and the read is refused -> read_json returns None. The supervisor watchdog treats a single None heartbeat payload as heartbeat_stale and cancels the whole workflow ('cancellation requested during pipeline'). Probe: tight replace-vs-strict-read loop hits the race on 42,025 of 1,407,059 reads (3%). Live: wf_6a7ad997c63a fired 3x (9-31 min in) with an external 0.1s sampler proving status=running and heartbeat fresh on every sample; a patched pin watchdog logged heartbeat_stale:payload-NoneType at the 4th fire. Parked/busy runs fire sooner because they rewrite these files more often. Fix surface: (a) read_private_text_bounded should retry once when fstat sees st_nlink == 0 on a just-opened fd (replaced-under-us is not tampering); (b) the watchdog needs retry + multi-sample grace on ALL bad reads, not just missing files; both belong to tasks WD/WDB (dlg-a2w heartbeat lease, dlg-m0q watchdog classification). Interim pin patch (retry + grace) is running the burndown workflow now; ~/.delegate is untouched.

DECISION (Trey): launcher burst-capacity policy for simultaneous child spawns
description: dlg-44w.7c — coordinator-writes-options-for-Trey item from the burndown plan. When a workflow fans out many children at once (parallel() with many items, or several workflows launching together), delegate spawns them near-simultaneously, which can spike subscription rate limits and local resources. NOTE: the Workflow layer already caps agent() concurrency at min(16, CPUs-2) per workflow, so this is specifically about the DELEGATE LAUNCHER's child-process spawn burst (across workflows / direct delegate calls), not the workflow agent() cap. Options: (1) SERIALIZE child spawns via an engine-side launch semaphore/queue — bounds burst hard, adds launch latency, more engine complexity and a new failure surface. (2) DOCUMENT a stagger recommendation (users batch/stagger via pipeline) — zero engine change, relies on user discipline, doesn't bound a misbehaving caller. (3) CONFIGURABLE SOFT CAP on concurrent child launches (default high/unbounded, opt-in lower per-profile or per-run) — bounds worst case without forcing serialization, modest complexity. COORDINATOR RECOMMENDATION: option 3 (configurable soft cap) — durable middle, no forced latency in the common case, a safety valve for bursts. Needs Trey's pick before implementation; not built this run.
notes: CUT 2026-08-27 under Trey's 'we are massively overbuilding — cut shit and ship shit' scope call. Trey DID pick option 3 (configurable soft cap) when asked, and that stands as the design of record if this is ever built. Not being built now: the bead cites no actual incident (its language is 'can spike', not 'did'), and the Workflow layer already caps agent() concurrency at min(16, CPUs-2). Also VERIFY-ON-MAIN: wp-2m8.34's two sub-bugs (codex preflight rejecting non-strict schemas pre-launch; parse_json_tolerant picking decoy brackets) claim fixed per the bead's own notes — repro-on-base, add regression tests if missing, report healed SHA to hq in #v2-hardening so wp-2m8.34 can close.

title: Lane health heuristics: zero-commit flag, stalled-stream kill, structured-retry pool roll
description: Wave-3 design bead. From deck-parity run observations: (1) a lane with zero commits at half its stage budget should be flagged (DP.16: 60 min, 7MB read-only output, zero commits); (2) a lane with zero tool calls and a stalled non-thinking stream for N minutes should be killed early, not run out its full timeout (DP.17: omp gemini lane emitted only backtick fences for 25 min); (3) a structured retry should route to the NEXT pool entry, not re-run the model that just failed structurally. Design-first: these are policy knobs on the workflow runtime; defaults must not surprise existing workflows.

title: Registry finalization lock contention: concurrent lanes crash _persist_final_progress
description: With 4 concurrent lanes registered in one source workspace, a cursor safe run's finalization timed out on .delegate/.registry.lock after 30.0s and crashed with TimeoutError in _persist_final_progress (runner.py:614 via _finalize_tracked_run). The child had completed its work; the run was left marked 'stale' and the CLI exited 1, so a successful review read as a failed launch. Finalization should retry/backoff well past 30s or persist a fallback record outside the lock; a completed child's output must never be reported as failure because of registry contention. Observed 2026-08-26, ship-cleanup fleet.
close_reason: Implemented configurable registry-lock budgets, atomic per-run finalize WAL fallback/replay with cancel precedence, launch pre-spawn contention failure, and regression coverage in commits 1eeada5 and 7ad0c85.

title: capabilities refresh misreports fingerprint_mismatch as requested_harnesses_not_installed
description:
resolve_harness_selector returns fingerprint_mismatch (harness_discovery.py) when the configured binary answers as a different known harness. That collapses to installed: false, so `capabilities refresh`/`setup` tell the user the harness is missing when it is actually present and running under the wrong identity. Confirmed still true against current code: capability_commands.py's requested_harnesses_not_installed path only checks record.get("installed") is True, with no separate branch for fingerprint_mismatch, even though a probeStatus field now exists in the schema (capability_commands.py, describe_payload.py, model_discovery.py).

The honest fix needs probeStatus as a closed, schema-validated enum ({ok, partial, missing, error}) persisted in the cache, distinguishing "wrong harness" from "missing" — design-first, not a quick wording change. Precedent: the CONFIGURED_SELECTOR_MISSING vs probe_missing split already in harness_discovery.py.

Source: docs/plans/deferred.md, "Still open after the sweep" (2026-07-25 sweep record).
close_reason: Implemented typed fingerprint-mismatch provenance through SelectorResolution, refresh attempts, and CLI diagnostics; real CLI proof is tests.test_capability_commands.CapabilityCommandTests.test_real_cli_refresh_surfaces_typed_identity_mismatch; commit 2923ba3.

title: Discovery cache keyed on auth profile can ping-pong across invocation contexts
description:
An agent sandbox resolves e.g. `codex` to a cmux shim under TMPDIR; a login shell resolves the same auth profile to /opt/homebrew/bin/codex. Same profile, two answers, one cache file, so two contexts can each invalidate the other's record and ping-pong indefinitely. Masked today because drift comparison uses configured selectors rather than resolved paths, but any future move toward resolved-path comparison walks straight into it. Not yet designed.

Source: docs/plans/deferred.md, "Still open after the sweep" (2026-07-25 sweep record).
close_reason: Reproduced base PATH/TMPDIR ping-pong, added bounded context-keyed cache migration plus serialized merge writes; real CLI proof is tests.test_capability_commands.CapabilityCommandTests.test_real_cli_context_refreshes_do_not_mutually_invalidate; commits 2923ba3 and 0bd5947.

title: Pooled worktrees with no run record can never auto-clean
description: Retirement and prune both key off a run record. Roughly 50 of the ~106 pooled worktrees have no registry entry at all, so they retain as record_missing and nothing in the system will ever remove them, no matter how long they sit. Found during the 2026-08-27 pool audit (evidence: docs/evidence/worktree-sweep-2026-08-27). This is the one remaining hole in the retirement story after e11ce27 (ledger dirt) and 0cf29a5 (prune liveness guard). Small. Needs a decision on what evidence justifies removing a tree nothing claims — absence from the registry is not by itself proof the tree is disposable.
acceptance_criteria: An orphaned pooled worktree (present on disk, no run record) has a defined, safe cleanup path, and the pool audit reports orphans distinctly rather than silently retaining them.

title: Flaky: test_structured_retry_timeout_exhaustion_reaps_every_workspace races 0.2s timeout vs 1s fake-harness sleep under load
description: tests/test_workflow_commands.py::test_structured_retry_timeout_exhaustion_reaps_every_workspace uses a real fake-codex subprocess with FAKE_CODEX_SLEEP_SECONDS=1 against timeout=0.2; under system load the timing race can flake (observed 1 spurious fail then 8/8 pass, 2026-08-27, right after a lane finished). Durable fix: make the timing margin robust (larger sleep/timeout separation) or gate the real-subprocess timing tests behind a serialized marker so they don't race under xdist load. Low priority; causes occasional spurious gate reds.
close_reason: Fixed in f505ec9: timing margins widened (timeout 0.2s→1.5s, fake sleep 1s→5s) alongside the macOS portability pass; deterministic-fail on loaded macOS reproduced, then 3x green after fix, full gate PASS both platforms.

title: Flaky: test_silent_running_harness_snapshots_as_running races atomic rename under parallel gate load
description: tests/test_end_to_end_tracking.py::EndToEndTrackingTests::test_silent_running_harness_snapshots_as_running fails intermittently under the full parallel gate with 'BoundedReadError: record file has 0 links' on .delegate/index.json (private_io.py:57). Passes 5/5 in isolation; failed 1x under full gate load 2026-08-27. Pre-existing (Wave-1 did not touch the test or the 0-links guard). Root cause: the bounded read of index.json races the harness subprocess's atomic rename — the reader holds the old inode open when rename unlinks it, so st_nlink==0. Durable fix: make the bounded reader retry once on st_nlink==0 (the rename is atomic, so a re-open gets the new inode) rather than raising, OR have the test synchronize on the write. Not a blocker for Wave-1 ship (unrelated pre-existing flake).

title: OMP behavior probe test picks wrong binary and deny tests pass vacuously on a dead lane
description: tests/test_omp_read_only_behavior.py resolves shutil.which('omp') which on the estate is the raw unbrokered binary (~/.local/bin/omp, default model fireworks/kimi-k2.7-code, invalid key -> instant 401), not estate-omp. The deny tests assert a file does NOT exist, so a lane that errors instantly passes them vacuously — observed 2026-08-27: full suite 'passed' the two deny tests in 2.4s against a dead binary; only the read test caught it. Also the omp default model (zai-glm-4.7) is archived, so even estate-omp needs an explicit --model. Fix: env override for the binary (e.g. DELEGATE_OMP_BEHAVIOR_BIN) + explicit model arg + guard deny tests against vacuity (require the same run's read probe to succeed, or assert turn_end stopReason != error before trusting a deny).

title: Mail tests break in shallow checkouts: tempdir at parents[3] of test file
description: tests/test_mail_*.py setUp creates its TemporaryDirectory at Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] — two levels above the repo root, deliberately outside the tree. title: Design and ship explicit worktree reap deletion verb
description:
`worktree gc --all` (shipped v0.21.0) only scans and reports orphaned worktrees whose source repo is gone — it deletes nothing, at any depth, by design. The actual reclamation verb was deliberately deferred: a separate explicit `worktree reap --older-than DAYS --yes` command with real pool-root validation. This is the lesson from the round-1 review blocker on the original sweep: `--pool PATH` (arbitrary user root) composed with empty-dir rmdir meant `gc --pool "$HOME"` could have removed home directories — each piece was safe alone, so the deletion verb needs its own careful design pass, not a flag bolted onto gc.

Related caveats to fold into this design rather than opening separate tickets (per the deferred doc's own instruction): source_root_missing records are permanently visible/unclearable since deletion depends on a live source that creation didn't require; and `_has_detached_backlink` can mislabel a non-worktree directory nested under an unrelated ancestor repo — cosmetic today, becomes load-bearing once a reaper acts on classification.

Source: docs/plans/deferred.md, "Still open after the sweep" (2026-07-25 sweep record) + worktree gc fixes #3/#4 section (v0.18.0).
notes: CUT 2026-08-27 with the rest of the W2-P worktree deletion-safety project. The 816-line r2 design is preserved on branch fix/w2-worktree-safety at commit d758391. Rationale: deletion was already conservative to a fault — the real defect was that the retirement dirty check counted our own instrumentation (.beads, .papercuts.jsonl) as user work, fixed in a few lines at e11ce27, and prune's missing liveness guard, fixed at 0cf29a5. An explicit reap verb solves a problem we no longer have.
